title: View config
description: How the configuration model is shown in one figure: display names, groups, aggregates, hidden elements, and the layout. It adds no facts: a label here is not evidence. Version 0.1.

$schema.description: Lets an editor bind this file to the schema. The tool keeps it and does not read it.

schema_version.description: The version of this contract, written in quotes: "0.1". Without the quotes YAML reads a number. A tool reads only the versions it supports.

view.description: The kind of figure. This version draws the overview.

title.description: The title of the figure, a string. Put it in quotes when it reads as a number, true, false, or null, or when it holds a number sign after a space, which starts a comment otherwise.

labels.description: Display names by ID. Each name here is the ID of a node or an edge of the model, in the ID form: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter. Each value is the role line of the node or the label of the relation. A label renames and is not evidence.

boundaries.description: Display names of real boundaries. A boundary is named through a node that sits in it.

groups.description: Logical groups, each drawn around its members. A group explains the figure and is not a real boundary.

aggregates.description: Aggregates, each drawn as one node in place of its members.

hidden.description: The IDs of the nodes and edges left out of the figure, each listed once. The model keeps them and their evidence.

layout.description: Where things are drawn. It never changes what is drawn.

id.description: A name in the ID form: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter. Put a name in quotes when it reads as true, false, or null.

nodeId.description: The ID of a node of the model.

elementId.description: The ID of a node or an edge of the model.

label.description: A string shown in the figure, of one character or more. Put it in quotes when it reads as a number, true, false, or null, or when it holds a number sign after a space, which starts a comment otherwise.

members.description: The IDs of the member nodes, one or more, each listed once.

boundaryAlias.description: The display name of one real boundary: member names a node in it, and label is the name.

member.description: A node that sits in the boundary.

level.description: Which boundary around the member is named: the one of its owner, such as an account or a project, the one of its region, or the one of its network, such as a VPC.

label.description: The display name of the boundary.

group.description: A logical group: an ID, a label, and the member nodes.

id.description: The ID of the group. No other group or aggregate, and no node or edge of the model, has the same ID.

kind.description: The view config can add logical groups only. Real boundaries come from the evidence in the model.

label.description: The name shown on the group.

aggregate.description: An aggregate: an ID, a label, and the member nodes it stands for.

id.description: The ID of the aggregate. No other group or aggregate, and no node or edge of the model, has the same ID.

label.description: The title of the aggregate node.

role.description: The role line of the aggregate node, a string. Without it the node says how many members it stands for. Put it in quotes when it holds a number sign after a space, which starts a comment otherwise.

layout.description: Where things are drawn: the layout engine, the direction, and the seed.

engine.description: The layout engine. tala lays the figure out by a seed; elk has no seed.

direction.description: The direction in which things are laid out. With elk, right tends to give a landscape figure and down a portrait one; with tala it depends on the model.

seed.description: Picks one of the layouts that tala can give for the same input: a whole number from 1 to 2147483647. The same model, view config, and seed give the same figure. elk ignores it.
